policies.title: Kosovo ordinary passports: Chile prior transient-stay visa
policies.summary: Chile's current 6 March 2026 transient-stay table expressly marks Kosovo [12] ‘SI’ in response to whether a visa is required. Chile's consular process requires application before travel and delivers an approved visa electronically for presentation with the current travel document.
conditions: The current table's Kosovo row is ‘KOSOVO [12] SI’, under the heading ‘¿REQUIERE VISA DE PERMANENCIA TRANSITORIA?’, with a maximum 90-day stay shown for simple and multiple visas.
Footnote [12] says Chile does not recognise the Republic of Kosovo as a subject of international law; the same table nevertheless expressly assigns the Kosovo row the prior-visa result.

The traveler applies through Chile's online Consular Services, uploads the current passport's personal-data page and other required documents, and is notified whether the application is approved or refused.

After approval and payment instructions, the consulate sends the visa electronically; the traveler must print it and carry it with a valid travel document at entry. Final admission remains subject to Chilean immigration control.
Work, residence, diplomatic, official, service, transit, invitation, third-country-document and other special routes remain outside this ordinary short-visitor classification.

application.label: Chile Consular Services online
steps: Complete the prior-authorization or visa application and upload the required documents through Chile's Consular Services platform.
If approved, follow the consulate's payment instructions; the visa is sent electronically and must be printed for entry with the valid travel document.

policies.title: Kosovo ordinary passports: Mexico prior visitor visa
policies.summary: Mexico's current INM graphic expressly includes Kosovo in its countries and regions requiring a visa. The accompanying INM guidance directs listed nationals to obtain the visitor visa at a Mexican consulate before travel.
conditions: The current INM page says nationals of the listed countries or regions must obtain a visa under any condition of entry; its embedded official graphic expressly lists Kosovo.

For tourism, business or other non-remunerated activities, the current INM guidance directs the traveler to apply at a Mexican consulate for a visitor visa without permission to perform remunerated activities.

At the immigration checkpoint, the traveler must present a passport or identity-and-travel document valid under international law and a duly issued, current and valid visa; this general document-validity condition remains applicable.

The page separately describes residence, third-country visas, APEC-card and crew alternatives; those conditional routes do not alter this ordinary Kosovo-passport baseline. Final admission, purpose and 180-day maximum remain subject to INM controls.
